items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: it was to him naturally, I turned, and he came down, and I think that Earl Fuller's jazz band was the first jazz band records that Columbia put out.

ctx.x: This is an interview on the 28th of June 1961 with Ed Kirkaby, who has been a booker in New York for many years, was the originator and booker of the California Ramblers, and I find that he has some acquaintance with New Orleans items, which I believe will make his story of interest to the archives of jazz music at Tulane University. Ed, what was your first acquaintance with New Orleans music? Where did you first hear a New Orleans group, do you think?

Well, the first New Orleans group that I heard was at Risenwebers, and that was the original Dixieland Jazz Band, which came up in 1917. I was with the Columbians, I said at the time, and I believe from the records, but my memory is very vague on the thing, that they made a couple of records for Columbia at that time, which for some reason or other were not put out. Victor finally signed them up, and the reception of the public was so great that Columbia tore its hair out and got after me, and got after me, who…

It may have been the first jazz band that was derived from the New Orleans, the original New Orleans jazz band, too, was it? Do you remember anybody else imitating the original New Orleans jazz band style?
